newsitem.title: FRANCE: Holidays, sport curtail French election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Holidays, sport curtail French election campaign.

text.p: If President Jacques Chirac had wanted to distract public attention from the snap parliamentary election he has called for May 25 and June 1, he could not have chosen a better time.
His opponents charge this was anything but an accident.
The month of May is littered with public and school holidays, and major sports or cultural events that traditionally take precedence over politics in the media.
Extreme-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen charged that Chirac had called a 20-day campaign of which 11 were public holidays including long weekends.
May 1, Labour Day, May 8, the anniversary of the end of World War Two, and May 19, Whitsun, are all public holidays.
Since the first two holidays fall on Thursdays, many workers will take a four-day long weekend, a tradition known in France as "faire le pont" (making a bridge).
In addition, schools are on holiday from May 7 to 14.
The calendar of major sports and cultural events is also heavily laden.

On the sports front, it includes the French rugby challenge final on April 27, rugby cup final on May 31 and soccer cup final on May 10, and the final stages of European soccer cups in which Paris Saint-Germain and Monaco are still in contention, plus the French open tennis tournament beginning May 26.

On the cultural side, a special jubilee 50th anniversary 12-day Cannes film festival begins on May 7. Film stars and directors often get almost equal time with politicians on television during the annual event.
Chirac will have at least two opportunities to shine on the international stage during the campaign.

On May 23, he will attend a special informal European Union summit in Maastricht, the Netherlands, called to give the drive to reform EU institutions a boost ahead of a decisive summit in Amsterdam in June.

On May 27, he hopes to host a summit in Paris in which the leaders of the 16-nation NATO defence alliance, including U.S. President Bill Clinton, will sign a partnership agreement with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, laying a foundation stone for the post-Cold War European security order.

That prestige event would fall conveniently between the two rounds of the French election. However there is still a question mark over that date because NATO and Russia have not yet finalised the document and serious issues remain for the next negotiating session on May 7.
